simple.meaning: חַמָּה (chammâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “heat ; by implication, the sun.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חַמָּה (H2535) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 30:28, with occurrences in Job, Psalms, Song of Solomon, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חַמָּה (H2535) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חַמָּה (H2535) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חַמָּה (chammâh) / H2535 is traced through Job 30:28, Psalms 19:7, Song of Songs 6:10, Isaiah 24:23 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

occurrences.englishText: I go mourning without the sun.
Yahweh’s law is perfect, restoring the soul.

Moreover the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, in the day that Yahweh binds up the fracture of his people, and heals the wound they were struck with.
